elements.element: Customer owns the Deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 provides that HDI assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in the defined Deliverables developed specifically for the Company or the Site.

elements.element: Customer owns the work product created for it.
elements.evidence: The assigned Deliverables expressly include materials and work product developed specifically for the Company or the Site.

elements.element: Vendor assigns its rights in the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: The present-tense language “HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest” supplies the required assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The assignment is limited to project-specific work developed under the Agreement, and Section 5.5 expressly states that HDI retains its pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to every item of Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence covers only HDI's identified pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how. It does not cover every possible category of Vendor IP, such as other pre-existing materials, patents or marks, and the absence of such other embedded IP is not demonstrable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site in connection with Deerskin Products, defined as Company Data; the clause also states that no such rights transfer to HDI.

elements.element: The ownership structure creates no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly disclaims joint ownership of the identified Company assets, assigns all rights in Deliverables solely to the Company, and retains the excluded technology solely with HDI.

elements.element: Vendor owns all generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains only tools that are both pre-existing and generally applicable. The clause does not clearly reserve to HDI generic tools developed during the engagement.

elements.element: Vendor owns all generic know-how.
elements.evidence: The retention is limited to pre-existing and generally applicable know-how and does not clearly cover all generic know-how developed during the engagement.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company receives ownership of the Deliverables, not an express licence to them. The only express licence is to specified retained HDI technology embedded in or needed to use the Deliverables.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence to the Deliverables is granted; the express use right applies only to specified retained HDI technology.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The modification right applies to specified retained HDI technology, not under an express licence covering the Deliverables.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The sublicensing right applies to specified retained HDI technology, not under an express licence covering the Deliverables.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the retained-technology licence is perpetual, there is no perpetual licence covering the Deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the retained-technology licence is irrevocable, there is no irrevocable licence covering the Deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Although the retained-technology licence is worldwide, there is no worldwide licence covering the Deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Although the retained-technology licence is royalty-free, there is no royalty-free licence covering the Deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits exploitation for Customer's business.
elements.evidence: The Company owns the Deliverables, but the fallback's requested business-use licence to the Deliverables is not operatively granted.

result.reason: The redline substantially implements the preferred ownership structure, but its embedded-IP licence is limited to specified categories of HDI technology rather than any Vendor IP embedded in the Deliverables. The fallback is not met as drafted because no licence to the Deliverables is granted and the reservation of generic tools and know-how is limited to pre-existing, generally applicable items. It is not minimal because it adds worldwide, modification and sublicensing rights beyond the preferred licence requirements, adds ownership provisions for Content and Marks, and rearranges unrelated provisions. The unrelated commercial terms remain operative and no direct contradiction is introduced, although the placement of Section 5.5 after Section 7.1 and the narrow, ambiguous retained-IP formulation reduce drafting quality.
